messages:
andrew: quick heads-up — on the raven-mini-v3-int4 canary (streaming enabled) we saw ~0.8% func_call outputs that are syntactically valid JSON but missing the closing brace or have an extra trailing comma. only happens when streaming chunks arrive with small final tokens.

sofia: hmm, only on int4 canary? or replicated on fp16?

andrew: replicated on fp16 at ~0.02% (much lower). int4 jump looks real. ran with batch=8, kvcache=on, continuous batching enabled.

maya: do you have an example log?

andrew: pasted one below — you can see stream cut mid-"args":

```
STREAM CHUNK 1: {"name":"call_api","arguments":{"url":"https://api.example.com/ingest","body":{
STREAM CHUNK 2: "user":"u123", "event":{
STREAM CHUNK 3: "type":"click"},},
STREAM CHUNK 4: "metadata":{}}

# final flush missing, client assembled as-is -> parse error (but some clients just tolerate trailing comma)
```

liam: interesting. could be quantization causing higher token entropy at suffixes so streaming ends mid-utf8 segment?

tess: do we see this with streaming disabled? what about assembling full text then parsing?

andrew: with streaming off, incidence drops to 0.1% for int4. so streaming interplay is big.

sofia: possible hypotheses:
- int4 kernel output jitter causing earlier EOS/stop-token placement
- continuous batching sometimes flushes incomplete KV prefixes when buffer hits size limit
- tokenizer boundary differences after quantization

maya: any correlation with sequence length or prompt templates?

andrew: higher for long prompts (>= 1024). also seems worse with our structured-output prompt that uses examples (multiple }")

craig: infra-bot — can you pull canary traces for model=raven-mini-v3-int4, stream=true, sample=last_7_days, group by batch_size?

infra-bot: pulling traces for query: model=raven-mini-v3-int4 AND stream:true AND timeframe:7d. returning grouped metrics (batch_size histogram + parse_fail_rate) — ETA 20s. :gear:

infra-bot: results: batch_size 1 => parse_fail 0.25%, batch_size 8 => 0.82%, batch_size 16 => 1.5%. kvcache disabled reduces failure by ~3x across sizes.

sofia: that pattern implicates batching and kvcache interaction. good signal.

liam: quick mitigation options:
- disable streaming for int4 canary and any new int4 models until fix
- add post-stream finalizer that buffers last N tokens and ensures well-formed JSON before emitting func_call (cheap attempt)
- add tolerant parser that accepts trailing commas / unclosed brace and defers to repair service

tess: operationally I'm for disabling streaming on canaries first. keep hosted customers unaffected for now. we should add telemetry tag streaming_suffix_entropy for subsequent runs.

andrew: agreed. planned steps:
1) disable streaming on canary cluster (done?)
2) run targeted microbench: batch sizes 1,4,8,16 with kvcache on/off, draft script in repo under /tests/struct-onboard/stream-suffix.sh
3) implement post-stream finalizer prototype in runtime (buffer last 32 tokens, ensure JSON completeness)

sofia: for the finalizer, beware added latency and unexpected double-counting of tokens. maybe only run finalizer when candidate parse fails initially.

liam: exactly — try optimistic stream-first, then on parse failure run final buffer + repair. can also call our json-repair lambda with the partial string.

maya: can we add a lightweight signature in the stream metadata so clients can request "wait_for_final":true? that way SDKs can choose to wait for final chunk for func_calls.

andrew: good idea. add header x-rw-wait-final. SDK change + runtime gating. SDKs can opt-in progressively.

evals-bot: scheduled job: run eval suite structured-toolcall-canary v2 against raven-mini-v3-int4 with streaming:false, and v3 with streaming:true+finalizer-probe. ETA: 2 hours.

tess: follow-up tasks assigned:
- andrew: run microbench + upload logs to /shared/struct-onboard/1719854321/
- liam: prototype streaming finalizer (PR draft)
- sofi a: add telemetry flag and dashboard tile
- maya: coordinate SDK opt-in header docs

andrew: starting microbench now. will post minimal repro snippets + flaky IDs. thanks all :thumbsup:

liam: ping me when logs uploaded, I'll kick off perf regression checks.

sofia: adding a note to the onboarding checklist: "run stream vs non-stream structured output pass"
